neighbours.label: a preposition (mostly ' at') tying a state to a point of time or level ('at the same time', 'the levels they were at'); the - pole is the other side, the coordinator in a sequence that predicts 'then/later' ('first X, then', 'sooner or')
fire: The film is funny and deeply sad at the same time.
The reservoir is close to the level it was at during the 2011 drought.
He was both proud and nervous at the same moment.
Unemployment is back to where it was at the start of the decade.
You cannot be in two places at once, no matter how hard you try.
The stock fell to the price it traded at before the merger.
She laughed and cried at the same time when she heard the news.
Temperatures returned to the values they were at last spring.
quiet: The film is funny, and later it becomes deeply sad.
The reservoir is much lower than it was during the 2011 drought.
He was proud first and then nervous a moment later.
Unemployment is lower now than it was when the decade started.
You cannot be in two places, no matter how hard you try.
The stock fell sharply soon after the merger was announced.
She laughed first, and then she cried when she heard the news.
Temperatures returned to normal values after last spring.
